thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Streaming decode p99 spike detected in us-west-2 cluster. Current p95=220ms (SLO=120ms), p99=1.9s (SLO=500ms). Affected route: /v1/stream/generate. Error rate stable. Auto-mitigation not triggered.
Ashley: Seeing it on dashboards too. Dash link: https://console/redwood/dash/streams?run=6923456789
Martin: Noticed a correlated tail pattern after a TRT kernel push ~36m ago (build id: trt-2026-03-15-34). Could be compilepath interaction with FlashAttention.
Kevin: Can someone grab recent node-level logs and `dmesg` for GPU pagefaults? I want to rule out paging.
Ashley: Attaching quick grep of relevant lines: ```
[03-15 15:02:11] gpu0: page fault handled, eviction=1
[03-15 15:02:12] nvlink: link flapped on gpu1
```
Ryan: Hmm eviction shows up but not massive OOMs. Also seeing increased KV cache misses on the streaming path (cache hit down from 82% -> 54%).
SRE-Lead: Important: customer-facing SLOs for Dedicated and Hosted flagged. Need impact assessment on top 10 tenants. Ashley, Martin, run a quick tenant impact scan.
Ashley: Running tenant-scan now: `./tools/impact-scan --route /v1/stream/generate --window 15m`
Martin: Output snippet: ```
tenant: acme-inc | 99th latency: 2.1s | errors: 0 | requests: 1200
tenant: beta-saas | 99th latency: 1.8s | errors: 0 | requests: 900
```
Ashley: Confirmed multiple paying customers hit p99 > 1.5s. Marking P1 potential.
incident-bot: INCIDENT created: #INC-2026-0315-6923456789 (priority: P1) - Paging and decode-tail latency.
Kevin: I want to know if this correlates with the `-O2 -fno-vec` compiler flag experiment on the TRT build. Martin, can you check the compiler flags for that build id?
Martin: Compiler args for trt-2026-03-15-34: `--cflags "-O3 -funroll-loops -march=skylake -mavx2"` and we enabled a custom kernel path for FlashAttention v2. No `-fno-vec` here.
Ryan: Could be kernel scheduling change (cuda driver + trt combo) causing micro-evictions and increased latency distribution tail. I can roll a small traffic shadow to a fallback variant (cpu-quantized) to check if latency improves.
Ashley: Please do the shadow. Route 5% of new streaming traffic to `model-a-quant-fallback` via routing rule. Use `redwoodctl route apply --route /v1/stream/generate --shadow model-a-quant-fallback --percent 5`
Ops-Bot: Executed: shadow rule applied at 15:10 UTC.
Ryan: After 10 minutes: shadow p95=140ms, p99=420ms. Significant improvement. Suggests inference kernel change is the culprit.
SRE-Lead: Good signal. Next step: rollback TRT kernel build on a small canary pool. Martin, prepare rollback PR for the trt build to previous known-good (trt-2026-03-12-19). Tag the PR with #INC-6923456789.
Martin: Drafted PR: https://git.redwood/inference/infra/rollbacks/PR-486. It reverts the kernel binary and the FlashAttention v2 enable flag. CI will run smoke tests (~5m).
Kevin: While rollback is pending, increase autoscaler headroom on streaming workers to reduce queuing for tail requests: `kubectl scale --replicas=+30 deployment/stream-workers-usw2` (ops runbook step 3).
Ashley: Scaling now. Observability shows queue length dropping by ~40%.
incident-bot: Pager silence scheduled for oncall rotation at 15:30 UTC for this incident (30m).
Ryan: Rollback CI passed on canary. Rolling out to 10% of nodes now. Command: `infra-deploy --build trt-2026-03-12-19 --subset canary-10pct`
Ops-Bot: Canary rollback applied to 12 nodes. Monitoring...
Ashley: Canary metrics trending: p99 on canary nodes back to 480ms, cluster-wide p99 slipping down from 1.9s to 1.2s after initial rollback step.
SRE-Lead: Proceed to roll forward rollback to 60% if metrics continue improving. Keep 40% as safeguard. Also open customer comms: draft note for impacted tenants.
Kevin: I'll prepare a short bulletin: "We observed a decode-tail latency regression after a kernel/tooling update. We've rolled back the kernel on a canary and are progressively rolling it back cluster-wide. No errors observed; request success rates unaffected. Next update in 30m."
Martin: Noting for postmortem: confirm whether FlashAttention v2 change altered memory access patterns for KV cache and whether altered kernel scheduling introduced eviction bursts. Collect perf counters: `nvidia-smi dmon` and `perf record` from affected nodes.
Ryan: Also schedule a controlled repro: replay a captured traffic sample through the new kernel in a staging env with perf hooks enabled. I'll coordinate.
Ashley: For now, the incident owner handoff: I'm going to sign out in 20m. @Ryan, you take primary after me unless SRE-Lead reassigns. Documented in the thread.
SRE-Lead: Acknowledged. Ryan becomes incident owner at 15:30 UTC. Keep postmortem checklist items in #postmortems and tag with INC-6923456789.
Ryan: Taking ownership. I'll watch rollbacks and update every 10 minutes. If p99 > 1s for more than 3 polling cycles, escalate to infra-eng for emergency kernel rollback to full cluster.
Ashley: Final quick note to @support: please hold any customer-impacting CS tickets until next bulletin. I'll add the impact table to status.redwood. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT update logged. Severity -> P1. Updates: rollback canary applied.
Ryan: (15:28) cluster p99 now 720ms, overall improving. Continuing rollout to 60% per SRE-Lead. Next update in 10m.
